title: AEP Ohio Data Center Tariff (Schedule DCT)

latestAction.text: Merits briefing concluded at the Supreme Court of Ohio in the Ohio Manufacturers' Association Energy Group appeal (Case No. 2025-1458); oral argument not yet scheduled as last reported.

summary: PUCO adopted a settlement on July 9, 2025 creating a data-center-specific tariff for AEP Ohio. New data centers above 25 MW must pay for at least 85% of subscribed demand under long-term contracts (load ramp plus 8 years), post collateral, and pay exit fees of three years of minimum charges. The order also directed AEP Ohio to lift its moratorium on new data center connections. The compliance tariff took effect July 23, 2025.
significance: The first data-center-only rate class in PJM's largest growth market outside Virginia, and a template other Ohio utilities (FirstEnergy, Duke, AES) are now copying. AEP Ohio says the tariff cut about 30 GW of initial interest down to 5.6 GW of signed contracts. That makes it the clearest real-world test of whether take-or-pay terms filter out speculative load.

summary: On April 30, 2026 the PUC voted 5-0 to adopt a nonbinding model tariff for electric distribution companies serving large loads above 50 MW individually or 100 MW in aggregate. title: PG&E application for approval of Electric Rule No. 30 (transmission-level retail electric service)

latestAction.text: CPUC Decision D.26-09-016 extended the statutory deadline in the proceeding through February 26, 2027.

summary: PG&E asked the CPUC to approve Electric Rule 30, which sets terms for customers, mainly data centers, taking retail service at transmission voltage. It covers who pays for transmission-level interconnection facilities and upgrades, and the financial security and refund arrangements. The ratesetting proceeding (ALJ Garrett Toy; Commissioner John Reynolds, assigned March 2026) remains active. An August 7, 2026 ALJ ruling sought comments on proceeding status, with replies due September 21, 2026, and the statutory deadline was extended to February 2027.
significance: Rule 30 is California's main framework for connecting and allocating costs for large data-center loads in PG&E's territory, where PG&E reports multiple gigawatts of data-center interconnection requests. It will determine how much of the transmission build-out data centers pay for versus other ratepayers.
